- _OUTLOOK: Draft a fully-formatted email into Outlook for Mac — opens a ready-to-review compose window, never sends. Drives classic Outlook via AppleScript with HTML content so paragraphs, bullet lists, and numbered lists render correctly; degrades to a plain-text mailto draft if only New Outlook is present. Pulls recipient addresses from CONTACTS.md and writes in Nick's email voice. USE WHEN draft an email, write an email to X, email X about Y, open a draft in Outlook, compose an email, reply to X, send an email (draft it for review). NOT FOR actually transmitting mail unattended (this is draft-only), Gmail/web mail (no Outlook desktop), or bulk/broadcast sends (use _BROADCAST). Mac only — requires osascript.
- Agents: Compose CUSTOM agents from Base Traits + Voice + Specialization, and manage predefined functional TEAMS. Traits combine expertise (security, technical, research), personality (skeptical, analytical, enthusiastic), and approach (thorough, rapid, systematic). ComposeAgent.ts merges base + user config, outputs unique prompt + ElevenLabs voice + prosody. Predefined teams: engineering, architecture, marketing, design, security, research, content, strategy — each YAML-configured with roles, tensions, and specialist members. Observer team variant: read-only oversight agents that vote continue/halt/escalate against the tool-activity audit log (high-blast-radius or unattended runs only). USE WHEN create custom agents, spin up agents, specialized agents, agent personalities, available traits, list traits, agent voices, compose agent, spawn parallel agents, launch agents, engineering team, architecture team, marketing team, design team, security team, research team, content team, strategy team, get the team on this, observer team, audit agents. NOT FOR ad-hoc swarms or TeamCreate coordination (use Delegation). NOT FOR single-threaded delegation without unique identities (use Delegation Task).
- ApertureOscillation: 3-pass scope oscillation that holds a question constant while shifting the scope envelope — narrow/tactical, wide/strategic, then synthesis — to surface design tensions invisible at any single zoom level. Requires two distinct inputs: the tactical target (what you're building) and strategic context (the larger system it serves). Pass 1 captures the component's own internal logic. Pass 2 reveals what the system needs it to be. Pass 3 finds where those views diverge — that delta is the output. Produces: design tensions, scope recommendations, and coherence assessments. Single workflow: Workflows/Oscillate.md. BPE-fragile — quarterly test recommended to verify smarter models don't naturally oscillate scope without prompting. Best integration point: Algorithm OBSERVE phase (before ISC) or THINK phase (before approach commitment). NOT a lens rotation (that's IterativeDepth) and NOT idea generation (that's BeCreative). NOT FOR deep incident causal chains (use RootCauseAnalysis) or assumption decomposition (use FirstPrinciples). USE WHEN aperture oscillation, oscillate scope, zoom in and out, tactical vs strategic, scope framing, design tension, architecture decision, feature fits system, system coherence check, local vs global design, build this inside that, wrong scope, design review, scope negotiation.
- Aphorisms: Manages a curated aphorism collection with full CRUD — content-based matching, themed search, thinker research, and database maintenance. Organizes quotes by author, theme, context, and newsletter usage history to prevent repetition. Four workflows: FindAphorism (analyze newsletter content, match themes, return 3-5 ranked recommendations with rationale), AddAphorism (parse quote + author, extract themes, validate uniqueness, update theme index), ResearchThinker (deep research on philosopher, add sourced quotes to database), SearchAphorisms (search by theme, keyword, or author). Database at ~/.claude/skills/aphorisms/Database/aphorisms.md — stores full quote text, author attribution, theme tags, context/background, source reference, and usage history per entry. Theme index supports 12+ categories: Work Ethic, Resilience, Learning, Stoicism, Risk, Wisdom, Truth-seeking, Excellence, Curiosity, Freedom, Rationality, Clarity. Supported thinkers: Hitchens, Feynman, Deutsch, Sam Harris, Spinoza, plus any requested author. Newsletter integration: tracks which quotes used in which issues to enforce variety; content theme extraction drives automated matching. USE WHEN: aphorism, quote, saying, find a quote, research thinker, add aphorism, search aphorisms, quote for newsletter, what did X say about, quotes about [topic], quote bank, find matching quote, quote collection, add this quote, check usage history. NOT FOR general creative writing or social media post generation — those go through dedicated writing/social skill…
- Apify: Scrape social media platforms, business data, and e-commerce via Apify actors — Instagram profiles/posts/hashtags/comments, LinkedIn profiles/jobs/posts, TikTok profiles/hashtags/videos/comments, YouTube channels/search/comments, Facebook posts/groups/comments, Google Maps business search with contact/review/image extraction, Amazon products/reviews/pricing, and general-purpose multi-page web crawling with custom pageFunction extraction logic. File-based TypeScript wrappers (scrapeInstagramProfile, searchGoogleMaps, scrapeAmazonProduct, scrapeWebsite, etc.) filter and transform data in code before returning to model context, achieving 95-99% token savings over direct MCP protocol. Parallel multi-platform queries via Promise.all for social listening dashboards. Lead enrichment pipeline: Google Maps → qualified filter → optional LinkedIn enrichment. Competitive analysis across Instagram, YouTube, and TikTok simultaneously. USE WHEN scrape Instagram, scrape LinkedIn, scrape TikTok, scrape YouTube, scrape Facebook, Google Maps leads, Amazon reviews, business intelligence, multi-platform social listening, competitive analysis, lead generation, social monitoring, Apify actors, web crawl, extract contacts. NOT FOR X/Twitter bookmarks (use a dedicated X-API skill) or progressive scraping (use BrightData).
- Art: Generates static visual content across 20+ formats via Flux, Nano Banana Pro (Gemini 3 Pro), and GPT-Image-1. Covers blog header illustrations, editorial art, Mermaid flowcharts, technical architecture diagrams, D3.js dashboards, taxonomies, timelines, 2x2 framework matrices, comparisons, annotated screenshots, recipe cards, aphorism/quote cards, conceptual maps, stat cards, comic panels, YouTube thumbnails, PAI pack icons, and brand-logo wallpapers. Named workflows: Essay, D3Dashboards, Visualize, Mermaid, TechnicalDiagrams, Taxonomies, Timelines, Frameworks, Comparisons, AnnotatedScreenshots, RecipeCards, Aphorisms, Maps, Stats, Comics, YouTubeThumbnailChecklist, AdHocYouTubeThumbnail, CreatePAIPackIcon, LogoWallpaper, RemoveBackground. SKILLCUSTOMIZATIONS loads PREFERENCES.md, CharacterSpecs.md, and SceneConstruction.md. --remove-bg flag produces transparent-background PNG (can produce black backgrounds — verify visually). Up to 14 reference images per request (5 human, 6 object Gemini API limit). Output staged to ~/Downloads/ for preview before any project directory copy. Nano Banana Pro uses --size for resolution tier 1K/2K/4K and separate --aspect-ratio. USE WHEN: art, illustration, diagram, flowchart, infographic, header image, thumbnail, visualize, generate image, mermaid, architecture diagram, comic, icon, blog art, framework diagram, D3 chart, remove background, wallpaper. NOT FOR video or animation (use Remotion). NOT FOR the user's personal portrait/headshot (use a dedicated headshot skill).
- ArXiv: Search and retrieve arXiv academic papers by topic, category, or paper ID — with AlphaXiv-enriched AI-generated overviews. Uses arXiv Atom API (no auth) for discovery and search across cs.AI, cs.LG, cs.CL (NLP/LLMs), cs.CR (security), cs.MA (multi-agent), cs.SE, and cs.IR. Supports title (ti:), abstract (abs:), author (au:), and category (cat:) search fields with boolean operators (AND, OR, ANDNOT); sorts by lastUpdatedDate or relevance; paginates up to 2,000 results per call with 3s rate limit between calls. AlphaXiv enrichment fetches markdown summaries from alphaxiv.org/overview/{ID}.md; full text from alphaxiv.org/abs/{ID}.md as fallback; 404 means summary not yet generated. Workflows: Latest (new papers by category), Search (topic/keyword search), Paper (single paper deep-dive by ID or URL). API returns Atom XML — parse with text processing, not jq. HTTPS required with -L flag; check published date not lastUpdatedDate for truly new submissions. Output: paper title, authors, abstract, AlphaXiv summary, and direct arXiv URL. USE WHEN arxiv, papers, latest papers, research papers, new papers, what's new in AI research, recent ML papers, paper lookup, arxiv search, find paper by ID, summarize paper, latest NLP research, latest LLM papers, multi-agent papers, cs.AI latest, AI safety papers, software engineering papers, information retrieval papers. NOT FOR general web research (use Research), extracting content from arbitrary URLs (use Parser), or cybersecurity annual report analysis (use AnnualReports).
- AudioEditor: AI-powered audio and video editing pipeline: Whisper word-level transcription (insanely-fast-whisper on MPS) → Claude segment classification (KEEP / CUT_FILLER / CUT_FALSE_START / CUT_STUTTER / CUT_DEAD_AIR / CUT_EDIT_MARKER) → ffmpeg execution with 40ms qsin crossfades and room-tone gap fill → optional Cleanvoice API cloud polish for mouth sounds and loudness normalization. Distinguishes rhetorical pauses from accidental ones. Breaths attenuated to 50% volume (not removed). Preview mode (--preview flag) shows proposed cuts without modifying audio. Aggressive mode (--aggressive flag) applies tighter filler detection thresholds. Polish step (--polish flag) uploads to Cleanvoice API for mouth sound removal and loudness normalization — confirm before cloud upload of sensitive content. Pipeline tools: Transcribe.ts, Analyze.ts, Edit.ts, Polish.ts, Pipeline.ts. Single workflow: Clean.md. Requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; CLEANVOICE_API_KEY optional for polish step. USE WHEN: clean audio, edit audio, remove filler words, clean podcast, remove ums, cut dead air, polish audio, trim recording, audio cleanup, cut stutters, edit interview recording, preview edits, aggressive clean. NOT FOR video composition or animation (use Remotion).
- BeCreative: Divergent ideation and corpus expansion using Verbalized Sampling + extended thinking. Single-shot mode generates 5 internally diverse candidates (p<0.10 each) and surfaces the strongest. Multi-turn mode expands a small seed corpus (5-20 examples) into a diverse N-example dataset for evals, training, or test sets. Research-backed: Zhang et al. 2025 (arXiv:2510.01171) — 1.6-2.1x diversity increase on creative writing, 25.7% quality improvement, and synthetic-data downstream accuracy lift 30.6% → 37.5% on math benchmarks. Seven workflows: StandardCreativity, MaximumCreativity, IdeaGeneration, TreeOfThoughts, DomainSpecific, TechnicalCreativityGemini3 for algorithmic/architecture work, and SyntheticDataExpansion for VS-Multi corpus growth. Single-shot output is one best response, not a ranked list; SyntheticDataExpansion writes a JSONL corpus to MEMORY/WORK/{slug}/synthetic-data/. Integrates with XPost, LinkedInPost, Blogging (creative angles), Art (diverse image prompt ideas), Business (offer frameworks), Research (creative synthesis), Evals and _PROMPTINJECTION (consume expanded corpora). Reference files: ResearchFoundation.md (why it works, activation triggers), Principles.md (core philosophy), Templates.md (quick reference for all modes), Examples.md. Applies Five Questions to every rule — Does Claude already do this? Contradiction? Redundant? One-off fix? Vague? — then classifies each as CUT / RESOLVE / MERGE / EVALUATE / SHARPEN / MOVE / KEEP. Two workflows: Audit (full system — reads all force-loaded files from settings.json, reports token savings estimate) and QuickCheck (single file, fast keep/cut/sharpen verdict). Outputs categorized report with estimated line and token savings. Core principle: less scaffolding = better output — every unnecessary rule competes for attention and degrades the rules that matter. Anti-fragile rules to KEEP: verification harnesses, ISC, data pipelines, specific DO/DON'T examples, tool preferences, routing rules. Fragile rules to CUT: CoT orchestrators, format parsers, retry cascades, numeric personality scales, abstract value statements. Requires loadAtStartup and postCompactRestore.fullFiles to stay in sync in settings.json — removing a file from one requires checking the other. NOT FOR general code simplification or refactoring (use simplify skill). NOT FOR attacking logical or strategic flaws in ideas (use RedTeam for that). Two workflows: FourTierScrape for single URLs, Crawl for multi-page site mapping (light crawl via scrape_batch loop up to 50 pages, or full crawl via Bright Data Crawl API). Always starts at Tier 1 and escalates only when blocked — Tier 4 has usage costs. Outputs URL content in markdown format. - Browser: Headless browser automation via agent-browser — Rust CLI daemon with persistent auth profiles for fast, scriptable, parallel browser work. Supports batch commands, network interception, device emulation, per-site profile auth (one-time headed login, headless forever after), and parallel isolated sessions via --session. Workflows: ReviewStories (fan out YAML user stories to parallel UIReviewers), Automate (load/run parameterized recipe templates), Update. Phase 1 (always): parallel scan of work.json session registry, session-names.json, MEMORY/WORK/ directory names, and ISA title grep — returns 5 most recent matches per source, loads top-3 ISA summaries (first 10 lines only). Phase 2 (only if Phase 1 returns fewer than 3 matches): PAI git history + current project git history. Reads MEMORY/STATE/work.json (task, phase, progress, effort) and MEMORY/STATE/session-names.json (sessionId, name); uses fd for directory scan with --max-depth 1 and Grep for ISA title matches in files_with_matches mode. Git history searched via `git log --oneline --all --grep` on both PAI and current project repo. Output: session slugs (newest first), ISA summaries (first 10 lines), commit hashes if Phase 2 ran. ## claude.ai Crypto.com
Crypto.com Exchange MCP Server - Real-time cryptocurrency market data and interactive widgets.

Available Tools:
- get_widget: Get any interactive widget by name (orderbook, trades, candles)

4. Get BTC 4h candles: get_market_candles(symbol='BTC_USDT', interval='4h', limit=100)

[Title] 
[Title] LIMSOC FEATURE BRIEF
[Heading1] Surf Risk Rating integration into LIMSOC 
BRIEF NUMBER
LIMSOC-BRIEF-LSV-2026-005
VERSION
1.0
AUTHOR
Flynn Young
DATE
26/06
[Heading1] SIGN OFF
FEATURE CATEGORY
 1 – Critical Operational Risk
 2 – High Impact, Recoverable
 3 – Moderate Business Impact
 4 – Low Operational Risk
 5 – No Operational Dependency
Name
Date
FEATURE OWNER
Name: _____________________
SENIOR MANAGER - CAPABILITY
David Potter
STATE LIFESAVING COMMUNICATION OFFICER
Nicholas Wood
[Heading1] 
[Heading1] Overview
[Subtitle] High level statement outlining the feature and any relevant background information
The Surf Risk Rating Assessment   ⟦C1028086222→ Integration  →C1028086222⟧feature introduces a structured risk assessment capability within the LIMSOC platform, enabling SLS members to capture local environmental and operational risk information in a consistent manner. Recent years have shown a need to record and utilise knowledge and covert data into intelligence. 
[Heading1] Problem Statement
[Subtitle] What problem are we solving? 
  ⟦C1597402713→ We do not have a way to record and calculate local risk, average scores across regions, notify on abnormal or exceeded parameters and then predict and display scores on maps and platforms. →C1597402713⟧
[Heading1] Impact
[Subtitle] Impact of solving the problem. Can also include impact if left unaddressed.
[ListParagraph]   ⟦C1352510523→ Standardise  →C1352510523⟧surf risk assessments across patrols
[ListParagraph]   ⟦C1261322657→ Improve situational awareness for both patrol members and operational roles. →C1261322657⟧
[ListParagraph] Provide historical reporting and trend analysis.
[ListParagraph] Enable proactive notification of elevated risks.
[ListParagraph] Support future predictive analytics and machine learning capabilities.
[ListParagraph]   ⟦C1857988762→ Improve operational decision making using real-time environmental intelligence. →C1857988762⟧
[Heading1] Proposed Solution
[Subtitle] How are we going to do it? This may have multiple options. 
Develop a Surf Risk Ratingmodule within LIMSOC that allows members to complete a risk assessment linked to patrol activities.
  ⟦C1409753805→ This solution will: →C1409753805⟧
[ListParagraph] Capture locally observed environmental hazards
[ListParagraph] Incorporate automated environmental data from external API’s
[ListParagraph] Calculate a overall Surf Risk Rating .
[ListParagraph]   ⟦C1817767128→ Display risk ratings across maps, patrols and summaries. →C1817767128⟧
[ListParagraph] Generate notifications when conditions are met
[ListParagraph]   ⟦C1761278601→ Support future predictive modelling using historical assessment data. →C1761278601⟧
[Heading1] Functional Requirements
[Subtitle] What the system does
Primary 
[ListParagraph] Create a form to capture locally observed data. 
[ListParagraph]   ⟦C444474806→ Keep forms overly simple – create the ‘path of least resistance’ for member’s ease. Target if <60 second completion time  →C444474806⟧
[ListParagraph]   ⟦C587503224→ Wrap in a general feature flag and then allow per unit/per patrol type.  →C587503224⟧
[ListParagraph] If enabled –   ⟦C1187551582→ show  →C1187551582⟧as not completed in an alert colour,   ⟦C1758496135→ until completed per unit.  →C1758496135⟧
[ListParagraph]   ⟦C9613063→ Allow automation of questions and weighting inside the solutions algorithm.  →C9613063⟧
[ListParagraph]   ⟦C576187967→ Show members a list of mitigators based on the score (like the Stinger Log) →C576187967⟧ 
[ListParagraph] Give assessment log a geospatial position. 
[ListParagraph] Link (many-to-one) assessment to a patrol ID. 
[ListParagraph] Add individual assessments to end of day patrol email template. 
[ListParagraph]   ⟦C2018293814→ Display scores on unit modals, maps and summaries.  →C2018293814⟧
Secondary 
[ListParagraph] Read local weather data closest to the unit from  ⟦C481422149→  various sources. →C481422149⟧ 
[ListParagraph]   ⟦C1901446092→ Use automatic data to augment the observed data. Consider pre-existing data from internal LIMSOC info such as Stingers Logs and similar.  →C1901446092⟧
[ListParagraph]   ⟦C397444014→ Average scores across a zone, then region, then state →C397444014⟧. 
[ListParagraph] C  ⟦C1355193095→ alculate impact based on current and previous population trends for that location  →C1355193095⟧
[ListParagraph]   ⟦C2042829336→ Generate notifications based on abnormal scores or out of parameter results.  →C2042829336⟧
[ListParagraph] Ability to report on historic data and trends. 
Tertiary 
[ListParagraph] Use forecast data to extrapolate future scores in a predicative nature. 
[ListParagraph]   ⟦C525265396→ Display data in a meaningful to patrols and end users.  →C525265396⟧
[ListParagraph] Notify or warn when a significant increase occurs or threshold   ⟦C115480171→ reached →C115480171⟧. 
[Heading1] 
[Heading1] 
[Heading1] Non-functional Requirements
[Subtitle] How well the system does it
[ListParagraph]   ⟦C643289605→ Assessment completion should take less than 60 seconds. →C643289605⟧
[ListParagraph]   ⟦C1488915941→ User interface should minimise user input →C1488915941⟧.
[ListParagraph]   ⟦C2068093177→ Support configurable scoring algorithms without software changes. →C2068093177⟧
[ListParagraph]   ⟦C289766456→ Integrate with existing LIMSOC mapping functionality. →C289766456⟧
[ListParagraph]   ⟦C800566529→ Scale to statewide deployment. →C800566529⟧
[ListParagraph]   ⟦C1018984826→ Support configurable feature rollout through feature flags. →C1018984826⟧
[ListParagraph] Ensure reliable API integration for environmental datasets.
[Heading1] Timeline
What is the required timeline of this feature. Consider each stage of the   ⟦C28751423→ process →C28751423⟧
[Heading1] Configuration requirements
What configuration is required prior to deployment? How significant is the workload?
  ⟦C176786217→ Should be no configuration as direction connection to SLSA current API.  →C176786217⟧
[Heading1] Risks
[Subtitle] Any risks that may come with implementing this feature
Risk

High completion rates

[Subtitle] Anything that we could consider in future to build on this feature.

[C1028086222] (Nicholas Wood) Suggest we just call it a feature, as we are doing more than just integrating and API, we are also building a User Experience.

[C1597402713] (Nicholas Wood) Can we flesh this out a bit more to articulate the current state of relying on the ops app? No feedback or persistence of scores? Limited Visibility and Tracability. Happy to talk through the details more if needed.

[C1352510523] (Nicholas Wood) Not sure if standardise is the right word here as I would suggest that most people are already using SRR. What this will enable is more adoption, and more integration with core workflows through a native experience.

[C1261322657] (Nicholas Wood) I think we should be more specific here about the wins for operational awareness. I would suggest this is mainly for members not on the beach.

[C1857988762] (Nicholas Wood) Will it improve it? Or make it more transparent/documented/traceable? The introduction of this feature isn't technically a change to the way we operate. (Ack that in practice it will mean alot more people use it).

[C1761278601] (Nicholas Wood) Is this going to be part of the first pass?

[C1409753805] (Nicholas Wood) Should we be saying something here that we are recreating the existing SLSA tool. I.e rebuilding the experience rather than rebuilding the tool which has alot of research backing?

[C1817767128] (Nicholas Wood) Is this part of the first pass?

[C444474806] (Nicholas Wood) Not sure this should be a requirement. Where is the 60 sec benchmark coming from?

[C587503224] (Nicholas Wood) Probably should be separate requirements. Feature Flag, Can be toggled per type. Is it unit type or patrol type?

[C1758496135] (Nicholas Wood) What does completed per unit mean?

[C1187551582] (Nicholas Wood) Show what exactly?

[C9613063] (Nicholas Wood) Could we have more detail for this?

[C576187967] (Nicholas Wood) Is this inline with the current tool? Where is the list of mitigators coming from?

[C2018293814] (Nicholas Wood) Break this out to be specific. Where, when, how.

[C481422149] (Nicholas Wood) So is the requirement to collate multiple sources? Or is one source ok?

[C1901446092] (Nicholas Wood) Should be specific as to what this looks like

[C397444014] (Nicholas Wood) What's the intended outcome here? Is an average score a useful metric?

[C1355193095] (Nicholas Wood) Where are the population trends coming from? What methodology are we using to determine impact?

[C2042829336] (Nicholas Wood) What are parameter results? How will we define abnormal?

[C525265396] (Nicholas Wood) Is this not something we would want in the first iteration?

[C115480171] (Nicholas Wood) Can we cite the source for this framework please and link to supporting documentation.

[C643289605] (Nicholas Wood) Why do we need this? How do we ensure this doesn't compromise quality? If this is a hard metric, what data is supporting it/ how are we going to ensure that we have the sufficient training/assessment?

[C1488915941] (Nicholas Wood) I feel like minimise input needs quantifying. What's the intent?

[C2068093177] (Nicholas Wood) This is functional, but also too broad, can we please refine and say specfically what we want?

[C289766456] (Nicholas Wood) This is functional, we also need to define how.

[C800566529] (Nicholas Wood) What does this mean? What would a not statewide deployment look like?

[C1018984826] (Nicholas Wood) Is this already covered by functional requirement?

[C28751423] (Nicholas Wood) Could we site the source for this please.

[C176786217] (Nicholas Wood) There are requirements for configurability that need to be considered ( feature flag, config per unit/patrol type). - Probably minimal, but no configuration contradicts the requirements.

# LIMSOC FEATURE BRIEF

## Surf Risk Rating in LIMSOC

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Brief number** | LIMSOC-BRIEF-LSV-2026-005 |
| **Version** | 2.0 (redraft) |
| **Author** | Flynn Young |
| **Revised by** | Nicholas Wood (State Lifesaving Communications Officer) |
| **Date** | 01/07/2026 |

---

## Sign off

**Feature category** (recommended: 3 - Moderate Business Impact. The SRR model itself is unaffected if the LIMSOC feature is unavailable, so this is high-value but not critical-path.)

- 1 - Critical Operational Risk
- 2 - High Impact, Recoverable
- **3 - Moderate Business Impact** *(recommended)*
- 4 - Low Operational Risk
- 5 - No Operational Dependency

| Role | Name | Date |
|---|---|---|
| Feature owner | _____________________ | |
| Senior Manager - Capability | David Potter | |
| State Lifesaving Communications Officer | Nicholas Wood | |

---

## Overview

*High-level statement outlining the feature and any relevant background information.*

The Surf Risk Rating (SRR) feature brings SLSA's established Surf Risk Rating assessment into LIMSOC as a native experience. SLSA already provides an SRR model with research behind its questions and weightings, and members already use it. What is missing is a native LIMSOC experience that captures each assessment against a patrol, retains it, surfaces it to the roles that need it, and feeds it into reporting.

This feature rebuilds the SRR *experience* inside LIMSOC and connects it to core patrol workflows. It does not build a new risk model. The scoring model, question set and mitigators are replicated from the existing SLSA tool exactly, so the research backing is preserved.

## Problem Statement

*What problem are we solving?*

Members currently complete the Surf Risk Rating in [**confirm current tool: SLSA Ops app?**], separate from LIMSOC. That leaves three gaps:

- **No persistence or feedback.** Assessments are entered but not retained against a patrol, so there is no record to review, compare against later conditions, or learn from.
- **Limited visibility and traceability.** Operational roles off the beach (field, dispatch, duty officers) cannot see whether an assessment has been completed for a unit, or what it found.
- **No connection to workflow.** The assessment sits outside patrol records and reporting, so it does not inform the operational picture or the end-of-day record.

In short, we have no way to capture the SRR against a patrol, retain it, surface it to the people who need it, and report on it.

## Impact

*Impact of solving the problem, including the impact if left unaddressed.*

- **Drive adoption and integration.** A native, low-friction experience embedded in existing patrol workflows increases uptake of the SRR and makes it part of how patrols already work, rather than a separate step.
- **Give off-beach roles visibility.** Field, dispatch and duty roles gain sight of local risk and of whether an assessment has been completed for each unit. This is the primary situational-awareness win, and it lands with members who are not on the beach.
- **Make risk assessment traceable and documented.** The feature does not change how we operate, but it makes the assessment persistent, reviewable and auditable rather than transient. In practice it will also mean many more people use the SRR.
- **Build the data foundation.** A retained, structured record is the prerequisite for the later reporting, trend analysis and predictive capability described in Future Improvements.

## Proposed Solution

*How are we going to do it?*

Rebuild the SLSA Surf Risk Rating experience natively within LIMSOC, replicating SLSA's existing SRR question set, weightings and scoring model exactly [**cite: SLSA SRR framework source**], and connecting it to patrol workflows. We are recreating the experience of a research-backed tool inside LIMSOC, not designing a new risk model.

The first pass (v1) will:

- Capture locally observed environmental hazards through the existing SLSA SRR question set.
- Prefill and augment the assessment with automated weather data from the Bureau of Meteorology (BOM) for the location nearest the unit.
- Calculate the Surf Risk Rating using the SLSA scoring model.
- Link each assessment (many-to-one) to a patrol/unit.
- Make each assessment reviewable from patrol, field and dispatch views.
- Include the SRR in the patrol report and allow export of an individual SRR.

Notifications, aggregation, map display and predictive modelling are deferred to later phases (see Future Improvements).

## Functional Requirements

*What the system does. Primary = first pass (v1). Secondary = phase 2. Tertiary = future.*

### Primary (v1 - first pass)

- Provide a capture form built on the SLSA SRR question set. Minimise friction: automate wherever possible, prefill from data already captured, and use engagement/gamification to encourage completion.
- Prefill and augment the assessment with BOM weather data for the location nearest the unit.
- Calculate the SRR score using the SLSA scoring model.
- Give each assessment a geospatial position.
- Link each assessment (many-to-one) to a patrol/unit.
- Make each assessment reviewable from **patrol, field and dispatch** views.
- Show members the mitigators associated with the score, sourced from the SLSA SRR framework [**cite source**] and presented like the Stinger Log. *(Confirm: keep in v1 as part of replicating the experience?)*
- Include the SRR in the patrol report.
- Export an individual SRR.
- **Feature flag:** a general on/off flag for the feature (see Configuration).
- **Per-unit and per-patrol-type enablement** (see Configuration). *(Confirm granularity: per unit, per patrol type, or both?)*
- Where enabled and not yet completed, show the unit in an alert colour until an assessment has been logged for that unit for the patrol period.

### Secondary (phase 2)

- Augment observed data with additional internal LIMSOC data (for example Stinger Logs and similar), beyond BOM.
- Generate notifications when a score is elevated or falls outside defined parameters. *(Parameters and "abnormal" to be defined in the phase 2 brief.)*
- Average scores across zone, then region, then state. *(To be defined against a clear, useful metric and outcome before committing.)*
- Display scores on unit modals, maps and summaries.
- Report on historic data and trends.

### Tertiary (future)

- Use forecast data to extrapolate future scores in a predictive nature.
- Weight impact using current and previous population trends for a location. *(Requires a data source and an agreed methodology.)*
- Present the data in a form that is meaningful to patrols and end users.

## Non-functional Requirements

*How well the system does it.*

- **Low friction.** The assessment should be as low-friction as possible: automate wherever possible, prefill from data already captured, and use engagement/gamification to drive completion. (No hard completion-time SLA; the intent is minimum friction, not a stopwatch target.)
- **Model fidelity.** Replicate the SLSA SRR scoring model faithfully. Hold the question set and weightings as configuration so changes to the SLSA model can be reflected without a code change.
- **Integration.** Integrate with the existing LIMSOC patrol, unit and reporting data model, and with the mapping data model to support later map display.
- **Reliable data.** Reliable BOM API integration, with graceful fallback to manual entry and override when data is unavailable or wrong.
- **Statewide use.** Operate for all units across the state under the feature-flag rollout, so the feature can move from pilot to statewide without rework.

## Timeline

*Required timeline, considering each stage of the process. (Dates to be set with the feature owner.)*

| Stage | Description | Target |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Confirm SRR model | Obtain and map the SLSA SRR question set, weightings, scoring and mitigators | TBC |
| 2. Build v1 | Capture form, BOM prefill, scoring, patrol/unit link, review views, patrol report, export | TBC |
| 3. Pilot | Enable per unit / patrol type via feature flag; validate adoption and data quality | TBC |
| 4. Statewide | Roll out under the feature flag across the state | TBC |

## Configuration requirements

*What configuration is required prior to deployment, and how significant is the workload?*

This feature does require configuration. A direct connection to the SLSA/BOM API is necessary but not sufficient, and "no configuration" would contradict the feature-flag and per-type requirements above.

- General feature flag to enable/disable the feature.
- Per-unit and per-patrol-type enablement.
- The SLSA SRR question set, weightings and scoring held as configuration, so SLSA model changes can be reflected without code changes.
- BOM data source configuration, including the location mapping for each unit.

Workload is expected to be modest. The scoring model is inherited from SLSA rather than designed from scratch, and the BOM connection is a standard API integration.

## Risks

*Any risks that may come with implementing this feature.*

| # | Risk | Impact | Mitigation | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Added friction reduces adoption | Members skip the assessment | Automate and prefill, keep to the SLSA question set, use gamification | High completion rates |
| 2 | BOM data inaccurate or unavailable | Incorrect or missing scores | Validate API data, allow manual override, graceful fallback to manual entry | Reliable scores |
| 3 | Divergence from the SLSA model over time | Loss of research backing / inconsistency | Hold model as configuration, govern against the SLSA source | Stays aligned with the research-backed model |
| 4 | Feature-flag / per-type config complexity | Difficult or uneven rollout | Clear config model, pilot per unit/patrol type before statewide | Controlled, staged rollout |
| 5 | Scope creep from deferred intelligence features | Delivery slips | This brief scopes v1 only; later capability is explicitly phased | Focused first pass |

## Future Improvements

*Anything we could consider in future to build on this feature.*

- Notifications on elevated or out-of-parameter scores.
- Aggregation and averaging across zone, region and state, once a useful metric and outcome are defined.
- Display on maps, unit modals and summaries.
- Population-based impact weighting, subject to a data source and agreed methodology.
- Forecast-based predictive scoring using historical assessment data.
- Broader augmentation from internal LIMSOC data (Stinger Logs and similar).

In short, we have no way to capture the SRR against a patrol, retain it, surface it to the people who need it, and report on it.

## Impact

*Impact of solving the problem, including the impact if left unaddressed.*

- **Drive adoption and integration.** A native, low-friction experience embedded in existing patrol workflows increases uptake of the SRR and makes it part of how patrols already work, rather than a separate step.
- **Give off-beach roles visibility.** Field, dispatch and duty roles gain sight of local risk and of whether an assessment has been completed for each unit. This is the primary situational-awareness win, and it lands with members who are not on the beach.
- **Make risk assessment traceable and documented.** The feature does not change how we operate, but it makes the assessment persistent, reviewable and auditable rather than transient. In practice it will also mean many more people use the SRR.
- **Build the data foundation.** A retained, structured record is the prerequisite for the later reporting, trend analysis and predictive capability described in Future Improvements.

## Proposed Solution

*How are we going to do it?*

Rebuild the SLSA Surf Risk Rating experience natively within LIMSOC, replicating SLSA's existing SRR question set, weightings and scoring model exactly [**cite: SLSA SRR framework source**], and connecting it to patrol workflows. We are recreating the experience of a research-backed tool inside LIMSOC, not designing a new risk model.

The first pass (v1) will:

- Capture locally observed environmental hazards through the existing SLSA SRR question set.
- Prefill and augment the assessment with automated weather data from the Bureau of Meteorology (BOM) for the location nearest the unit.
- Calculate the Surf Risk Rating using the SLSA scoring model.
- Link each assessment (many-to-one) to a patrol/unit.
- Make each assessment reviewable from patrol, field and dispatch views.
- Include the SRR in the patrol report and allow export of an individual SRR.

Notifications, aggregation, map display and predictive modelling are deferred to later phases (see Future Improvements).

## Functional Requirements

*What the system does. Primary = first pass (v1). Secondary = phase 2. Tertiary = future.*

### Primary (v1 - first pass)

- Provide a capture form built on the SLSA SRR question set. Minimise friction: automate wherever possible, prefill from data already captured, and use engagement/gamification to encourage completion.
- Prefill and augment the assessment with BOM weather data for the location nearest the unit.
- Calculate the SRR score using the SLSA scoring model.
- Give each assessment a geospatial position.
- Link each assessment (many-to-one) to a patrol/unit.
- Make each assessment reviewable from **patrol, field and dispatch** views.
- Show members the mitigators associated with the score, sourced from the SLSA SRR framework [**cite source**] and presented like the Stinger Log. *(Confirm: keep in v1 as part of replicating the experience?)*
- Include the SRR in the patrol report.
- Export an individual SRR.
- **Feature flag:** a general on/off flag for the feature (see Configuration).
- **Per-unit and per-patrol-type enablement** (see Configuration). *(Confirm granularity: per unit, per patrol type, or both?)*
- Where enabled and not yet completed, show the unit in an alert colour until an assessment has been logged for that unit for the patrol period.

### Secondary (phase 2)

- Augment observed data with additional internal LIMSOC data (for example Stinger Logs and similar), beyond BOM.
- Generate notifications when a score is elevated or falls outside defined parameters. *(Parameters and "abnormal" to be defined in the phase 2 brief.)*
- Average scores across zone, then region, then state. *(To be defined against a clear, useful metric and outcome before committing.)*
- Display scores on unit modals, maps and summaries.
- Report on historic data and trends.

### Tertiary (future)

- Use forecast data to extrapolate future scores in a predictive nature.
- Weight impact using current and previous population trends for a location. *(Requires a data source and an agreed methodology.)*
- Present the data in a form that is meaningful to patrols and end users.

## Non-functional Requirements

*How well the system does it.*

- **Low friction.** The assessment should be as low-friction as possible: automate wherever possible, prefill from data already captured, and use engagement/gamification to drive completion. (No hard completion-time SLA; the intent is minimum friction, not a stopwatch target.)
- **Model fidelity.** Replicate the SLSA SRR scoring model faithfully. Hold the question set and weightings as configuration so changes to the SLSA model can be reflected without a code change.
- **Integration.** Integrate with the existing LIMSOC patrol, unit and reporting data model, and with the mapping data model to support later map display.
- **Reliable data.** Reliable BOM API integration, with graceful fallback to manual entry and override when data is unavailable or wrong.
- **Statewide use.** Operate for all units across the state under the feature-flag rollout, so the feature can move from pilot to statewide without rework.

## Timeline

*Required timeline, considering each stage of the process. (Dates to be set with the feature owner.)*

| Stage | Description | Target |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Confirm SRR model | Obtain and map the SLSA SRR question set, weightings, scoring and mitigators | TBC |
| 2. Build v1 | Capture form, BOM prefill, scoring, patrol/unit link, review views, patrol report, export | TBC |
| 3. Pilot | Enable per unit / patrol type via feature flag; validate adoption and data quality | TBC |
| 4. Statewide | Roll out under the feature flag across the state | TBC |

## Configuration requirements

*What configuration is required prior to deployment, and how significant is the workload?*

This feature does require configuration. A direct connection to the SLSA/BOM API is necessary but not sufficient, and "no configuration" would contradict the feature-flag and per-type requirements above.

- General feature flag to enable/disable the feature.
- Per-unit and per-patrol-type enablement.
- The SLSA SRR question set, weightings and scoring held as configuration, so SLSA model changes can be reflected without code changes.
- BOM data source configuration, including the location mapping for each unit.

Workload is expected to be modest. The scoring model is inherited from SLSA rather than designed from scratch, and the BOM connection is a standard API integration.

## Risks

*Any risks that may come with implementing this feature.*

| # | Risk | Impact | Mitigation | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Added friction reduces adoption | Members skip the assessment | Automate and prefill, keep to the SLSA question set, use gamification | High completion rates |
| 2 | BOM data inaccurate or unavailable | Incorrect or missing scores | Validate API data, allow manual override, graceful fallback to manual entry | Reliable scores |
| 3 | Divergence from the SLSA model over time | Loss of research backing / inconsistency | Hold model as configuration, govern against the SLSA source | Stays aligned with the research-backed model |
| 4 | Feature-flag / per-type config complexity | Difficult or uneven rollout | Clear config model, pilot per unit/patrol type before statewide | Controlled, staged rollout |
| 5 | Scope creep from deferred intelligence features | Delivery slips | This brief scopes v1 only; later capability is explicitly phased | Focused first pass |

## Future Improvements

*Anything we could consider in future to build on this feature.*

- Notifications on elevated or out-of-parameter scores.
- Aggregation and averaging across zone, region and state, once a useful metric and outcome are defined.
- Display on maps, unit modals and summaries.
- Population-based impact weighting, subject to a data source and agreed methodology.
- Forecast-based predictive scoring using historical assessment data.
- Broader augmentation from internal LIMSOC data (Stinger Logs and similar).

file.content:
The Surf Risk Rating (SRR) feature brings SLSA's established Surf Risk Rating assessment into LIMSOC as a native experience. SLSA already provides an SRR model with research behind its questions and weightings, and members already use it. What is missing is a native LIMSOC experience that captures each assessment against a patrol, retains it, surfaces it to the roles that need it, and feeds it into reporting.

This feature rebuilds the SRR *experience* inside LIMSOC and connects it to core patrol workflows. It does not build a new risk model. The scoring model, question set and mitigators are replicated from the existing SLSA tool exactly, so the research backing is preserved.

## Problem Statement

*What problem are we solving?*

Members currently complete the Surf Risk Rating in [**confirm current tool: SLSA Ops app?**], separate from LIMSOC. That leaves three gaps:

- **No persistence or feedback.** Assessments are entered but not retained against a patrol, so there is no record to review, compare against later conditions, or learn from.
- **Limited visibility and traceability.** Operational roles off the beach (field, dispatch, duty officers) cannot see whether an assessment has been completed for a unit, or what it found.
- **No connection to workflow.** The assessment sits outside patrol records and reporting, so it does not inform the operational picture or the end-of-day record.

In short, we have no way to capture the SRR against a patrol, retain it, surface it to the people who need it, and report on it.

## Impact

*Impact of solving the problem, including the impact if left unaddressed.*

- **Drive adoption and integration.** A native, low-friction experience embedded in existing patrol workflows increases uptake of the SRR and makes it part of how patrols already work, rather than a separate step.
- **Give off-beach roles visibility.** Field, dispatch and duty roles gain sight of local risk and of whether an assessment has been completed for each unit. This is the primary situational-awareness win, and it lands with members who are not on the beach.
- **Make risk assessment traceable and documented.** The feature does not change how we operate, but it makes the assessment persistent, reviewable and auditable rather than transient. In practice it will also mean many more people use the SRR.
- **Build the data foundation.** A retained, structured record is the prerequisite for the later reporting, trend analysis and predictive capability described in Future Improvements.

## Proposed Solution

*How are we going to do it?*

Rebuild the SLSA Surf Risk Rating experience natively within LIMSOC, replicating SLSA's existing SRR question set, weightings and scoring model exactly [**cite: SLSA SRR framework source**], and connecting it to patrol workflows. We are recreating the experience of a research-backed tool inside LIMSOC, not designing a new risk model.

The first pass (v1) will:

- Capture locally observed environmental hazards through the existing SLSA SRR question set.
- Prefill and augment the assessment with automated weather data from the Bureau of Meteorology (BOM) for the location nearest the unit.
- Calculate the Surf Risk Rating using the SLSA scoring model.
- Link each assessment (many-to-one) to a patrol/unit.
- Make each assessment reviewable from patrol, field and dispatch views.
- Include the SRR in the patrol report and allow export of an individual SRR.

Notifications, aggregation, map display and predictive modelling are deferred to later phases (see Future Improvements).

## Functional Requirements

*What the system does. Primary = first pass (v1). Secondary = phase 2. Tertiary = future.*

### Primary (v1 - first pass)

- Provide a capture form built on the SLSA SRR question set. Minimise friction: automate wherever possible, prefill from data already captured, and use engagement/gamification to encourage completion.
- Prefill and augment the assessment with BOM weather data for the location nearest the unit.
- Calculate the SRR score using the SLSA scoring model.
- Give each assessment a geospatial position.
- Link each assessment (many-to-one) to a patrol/unit.
- Make each assessment reviewable from **patrol, field and dispatch** views.
- Show members the mitigators associated with the score, sourced from the SLSA SRR framework [**cite source**] and presented like the Stinger Log. *(Confirm: keep in v1 as part of replicating the experience?)*
- Include the SRR in the patrol report.
- Export an individual SRR.
- **Feature flag:** a general on/off flag for the feature (see Configuration).
- **Per-unit and per-patrol-type enablement** (see Configuration). *(Confirm granularity: per unit, per patrol type, or both?)*

The headline count barely moved (26 → 25), but that's the wrong way to read it. What changed is the *composition*:

We will then own the persistence of this and the linking to a patrol. There also needs to be assumption about the SLSA API will be performant and reliable (they have a history of doing neither). We also need to define the behaviour in the case that the API is not available. The form should be blocked if we don't get a healthy response from the API. Another assumption probably needs to be a health check endpoint.

This is a material architecture correction — thank you, it changes the brief meaningfully. To be explicit about what I now understand (and where I had it backwards):

**SLSA owns the engine, not us.** LIMSOC builds the form, collects the inputs, passes them to the SLSA API, and receives the score, rating and mitigation list back. We own persistence of that result, the patrol/unit link, the review views and reporting. My earlier "replicate the model as owned configuration" framing was wrong and I'm reversing it — there *is* a hard runtime dependency on the SLSA API.

That brings four assumptions and a fail-behaviour requirement: (1) SLSA API is the scoring engine; (2) it returns score/rating/mitigants; (3) it's performant and reliable (flagged as risky, given their history); (4) a health-check endpoint exists — and the form must be **blocked** when the API isn't healthy.

Let me read the current file and rework the affected sections.

## Overview

*High-level statement outlining the feature and any relevant background information.*

The Surf Risk Rating (SRR) feature brings SLSA's established Surf Risk Rating assessment into LIMSOC as a native experience. SLSA already provides an SRR model with research behind its questions and weightings, and members already use it. What is missing is a native LIMSOC experience that captures each assessment against a patrol, retains it, surfaces it to the roles that need it, and feeds it into reporting.

This feature rebuilds the SRR *experience* inside LIMSOC and connects it to core patrol workflows. It does not build a new risk model. The scoring model, question set and mitigants are replicated exactly from SLSA's Surf Risk Rating tool in the SLSA Operations App, so the research backing is preserved.

## Problem Statement

*What problem are we solving?*

Members currently complete the Surf Risk Rating in the SLSA Operations App, separate from LIMSOC. That leaves three gaps:

- **No persistence or feedback.** Assessments are entered but not retained against a patrol, so there is no record to review, compare against later conditions, or learn from.
- **Limited visibility and traceability.** Operational roles off the beach (field, dispatch, duty officers) cannot see whether an assessment has been completed for a unit, or what it found.
- **No connection to workflow.** The assessment sits outside patrol records and reporting, so it does not inform the operational picture or the end-of-day record.

In short, we have no way to capture the SRR against a patrol, retain it, surface it to the people who need it, and report on it.

## Impact

*Impact of solving the problem, including the impact if left unaddressed.*

- **Drive adoption and integration.** A native, low-friction experience embedded in existing patrol workflows increases uptake of the SRR and makes it part of how patrols already work, rather than a separate step.
- **Give off-beach roles visibility.** Field, dispatch and duty roles gain sight of local risk and of whether an assessment has been completed for each unit. This is the primary situational-awareness win, and it lands with members who are not on the beach.
- **Make risk assessment traceable and documented.** The feature does not change how we operate, but it makes the assessment persistent, reviewable and auditable rather than transient. In practice it will also mean many more people use the SRR.
- **Build the data foundation.** A retained, structured record is the prerequisite for the later reporting, trend analysis and predictive capability described in Future Improvements.

## Proposed Solution

*How are we going to do it?*

Rebuild the SLSA Surf Risk Rating experience natively within LIMSOC, replicating the question set, weightings, scoring and mitigants defined by SLSA's Surf Risk Rating tool in the SLSA Operations App, and connecting it to patrol workflows. We are recreating the experience of a research-backed tool inside LIMSOC, not designing a new risk model. The SLSA model definition is a delivery dependency (see Configuration requirements).

The first pass (v1) will:

- Capture locally observed environmental hazards through the existing SLSA SRR question set.
- Prefill and augment the assessment with automated weather data from the Bureau of Meteorology (BOM) for the location nearest the unit.
- Calculate the Surf Risk Rating using the SLSA scoring model.
- Link each assessment (many-to-one) to a patrol/unit.
- Make each assessment reviewable from patrol, field and dispatch views.
- Include the SRR in the patrol report and allow export of an individual SRR.

Notifications, aggregation, map display and predictive modelling are deferred to later phases (see Future Improvements).

## Functional Requirements

*What the system does. Primary = first pass (v1). Secondary = phase 2. Tertiary = future.*

### Primary (v1 - first pass)

- Provide a capture form built on the SLSA SRR question set. Minimise friction: automate wherever possible, prefill from data already captured, and use engagement/gamification to encourage completion.
- Prefill and augment the assessment with BOM weather data for the location nearest the unit.
- Calculate the SRR score using the SLSA scoring model.
- Give each assessment a geospatial position.
- Link each assessment (many-to-one) to a patrol/unit.
- Make each assessment reviewable from **patrol, field and dispatch** views.
- Present the mitigants for the resulting rating, listed at the end of the assessment. The mitigants are those defined by SLSA's Surf Risk Rating tool, presented like the Stinger Log.
- Include the SRR in the patrol report.
- Export an individual SRR.
- **Feature flag:** a general on/off flag for the feature (see Configuration).
- **Per-patrol-type enablement:** enable or disable the feature by patrol type (see Configuration).
- Where enabled and not yet completed, show the unit in an alert colour until an assessment has been logged for that unit for the patrol period.

### Secondary (phase 2)

- Augment observed data with additional internal LIMSOC data (for example Stinger Logs and similar), beyond BOM.
- Generate notifications when a score is elevated or falls outside defined parameters. *(Parameters and "abnormal" to be defined in the phase 2 brief.)*
- Average scores across zone, then region, then state. *(To be defined against a clear, useful metric and outcome before committing.)*
- Display scores on unit modals, maps and summaries.
- Report on historic data and trends.

### Tertiary (future)

- Use forecast data to extrapolate future scores in a predictive nature.
- Weight impact using current and previous population trends for a location. *(Requires a data source and an agreed methodology.)*
- Present the data in a form that is meaningful to patrols and end users.

## Non-functional Requirements

*How well the system does it.*

- **Low friction.** The assessment should be as low-friction as possible: automate wherever possible, prefill from data already captured, and use engagement/gamification to drive completion. (No hard completion-time SLA; the intent is minimum friction, not a stopwatch target.)
- **Model fidelity.** Replicate the SLSA SRR scoring model faithfully. Hold the question set and weightings as configuration so changes to the SLSA model can be reflected without a code change.
- **Integration.** Integrate with the existing LIMSOC patrol, unit and reporting data model, and with the mapping data model to support later map display.
- **Reliable data.** Reliable BOM API integration, with graceful fallback to manual entry and override when data is unavailable or wrong.
- **Statewide use.** Operate for all units across the state under the feature-flag rollout, so the feature can move from pilot to statewide without rework.

## Timeline

*Required timeline, considering each stage of the process. (Dates to be set with the feature owner.)*

| Stage | Description | Target |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Confirm SRR model | Obtain and map the SLSA SRR question set, weightings, scoring and mitigators | TBC |
| 2. Build v1 | Capture form, BOM prefill, scoring, patrol/unit link, review views, patrol report, export | TBC |
| 3. Pilot | Enable per patrol type via feature flag; validate adoption and data quality | TBC |
| 4. Statewide | Roll out under the feature flag across the state | TBC |

## Configuration requirements

*What configuration is required prior to deployment, and how significant is the workload?*

This feature does require configuration. "No configuration" would contradict the feature-flag and per-patrol-type requirements above.

- General feature flag to enable/disable the feature.
- Per-patrol-type enablement.
- The SLSA SRR question set, weightings, scoring and mitigants held as configuration, so the SLSA model can be replicated and any SLSA changes reflected without code changes.
- BOM data source configuration, including the location mapping for each unit.

**Delivery dependency.** The SLSA SRR model definition (question set, weightings, scoring and mitigants) must be obtained from SLSA to populate this configuration. We do not currently hold SLSA's API or model documentation, so this is a prerequisite for Stage 1. Holding the model as owned configuration avoids a hard runtime dependency on an SLSA API.

Workload is expected to be modest. The scoring model is inherited from SLSA rather than designed from scratch, and the BOM connection is a standard API integration.

## Risks

*Any risks that may come with implementing this feature.*

| # | Risk | Impact | Mitigation | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Added friction reduces adoption | Members skip the assessment | Automate and prefill, keep to the SLSA question set, use gamification | High completion rates |
| 2 | BOM data inaccurate or unavailable | Incorrect or missing scores | Validate API data, allow manual override, graceful fallback to manual entry | Reliable scores |
| 3 | Divergence from the SLSA model over time | Loss of research backing / inconsistency | Hold model as configuration, govern against the SLSA source | Stays aligned with the research-backed model |
| 4 | Feature-flag / per-patrol-type config complexity | Difficult or uneven rollout | Clear config model, pilot per patrol type before statewide | Controlled, staged rollout |
| 5 | Scope creep from deferred intelligence features | Delivery slips | This brief scopes v1 only; later capability is explicitly phased | Focused first pass |
| 6 | SLSA SRR model definition not yet available to us | Cannot build to the exact model; Stage 1 blocked | Obtain the SLSA model definition early; hold it as owned configuration rather than depending on an SLSA API | Faithful replication, no runtime SLSA dependency |

## Future Improvements

input.old_string:

## Functional Requirements
input.new_string:
Notifications, aggregation, map display and predictive modelling are deferred to later phases (see Future Improvements).

## Assumptions

*What must hold true for this feature to work as described. Several centre on the SLSA API, which is the scoring engine.*

- **SLSA owns the engine; LIMSOC owns the form and the record.** LIMSOC does not build or hold the scoring logic. The form collects the inputs, passes them to the SLSA API, and the SLSA API returns the score, rating and mitigation list. LIMSOC then owns persistence of that result and the link to a patrol.
- **The SLSA API returns the score, rating and mitigation list.** The response contains all three, so LIMSOC does not need to derive any of them.
- **The SLSA API is performant and reliable.** This is assumed but not proven. SLSA has a history of APIs that are neither, so this assumption carries material risk and drives the fail-behaviour below.
- **A health-check endpoint is available on the SLSA API.** LIMSOC can query it to determine availability before allowing an assessment.
- **Fail behaviour: the form is blocked without a healthy SLSA response.** If the health check fails or the API does not return a healthy response, the assessment form is blocked and a clear unavailable state is shown. LIMSOC does not accept an assessment it cannot score, so no un-scored or locally-guessed assessments are recorded.

## Functional Requirements

2	
3	## Surf Risk Rating in LIMSOC
4	
5	| Field | Detail |
6	|---|---|
7	| **Brief number** | LIMSOC-BRIEF-LSV-2026-005 |
8	| **Version** | 2.0 (redraft) |
9	| **Author** | Flynn Young |

11	| **Date** | 01/07/2026 |
12	
13	---
14	
15	## Sign off
16	
17	**Feature category: 3 - Moderate Business Impact.** 
18	
19	- 1 - Critical Operational Risk
20	- 2 - High Impact, Recoverable
21	- **3 - Moderate Business Impact** *(selected)*
22	- 4 - Low Operational Risk
23	- 5 - No Operational Dependency
24

26	|---|---|---|

28	| Senior Manager - Capability | David Potter | |
29	| State Lifesaving Communications Officer | Nicholas Wood | |

31	---
32	
33	## Overview
34	
35	*High-level statement outlining the feature and any relevant background information.*
36	
37	The Surf Risk Rating (SRR) feature brings SLSA's established Surf Risk Rating assessment into LIMSOC as a native experience. SLSA already provides an SRR model with research behind its questions and weightings, and members already use it. What is missing is a native LIMSOC experience that captures each assessment against a patrol, retains it, surfaces it to the roles that need it, and feeds it into reporting.
38	
39	This feature rebuilds the SRR *experience* inside LIMSOC and connects it to core patrol workflows. It does not build the scoring engine. LIMSOC collects the assessment inputs, passes them to SLSA's Surf Risk Rating API, and presents the score, rating and mitigants the API returns. SLSA owns the model and the research behind it; LIMSOC owns the experience, the persistence of each result, and the link to a patrol.
40	
41	## Problem Statement
42	
43	*What problem are we solving?*
44	
45	Members currently complete the Surf Risk Rating in the SLSA Operations App, separate from LIMSOC. That leaves three gaps:
46	
47	- **No persistence or feedback.** Assessments are entered but not retained against a patrol, so there is no record to review, compare against later conditions, or learn from.
48	- **Limited visibility and traceability.** Operational roles off the beach (field, dispatch, duty officers) cannot see whether an assessment has been completed for a unit, or what it found.
49	- **No connection to workflow.** The assessment sits outside patrol records and reporting, so it does not inform the operational picture or the end-of-day record.
50	
51	In short, we have no way to capture the SRR against a patrol, retain it, surface it to the people who need it, and report on it.
52	
53	## Impact
54	
55	*Impact of solving the problem, including the impact if left unaddressed.*
56	
57	- **Drive adoption and integration.** A native, low-friction experience embedded in existing patrol workflows increases uptake of the SRR and makes it part of how patrols already work, rather than a separate step.
58	- **Give off-beach roles visibility.** Field, dispatch and duty roles gain sight of local risk and of whether an assessment has been completed for each unit. This is the primary situational-awareness win, and it lands with members who are not on the beach.
59	- **Make risk assessment traceable and documented.** The feature does not change how we operate, but it makes the assessment persistent, reviewable and auditable rather than transient. In practice it will also mean many more people use the SRR.
60	- **Build the data foundation.** A retained, structured record is the prerequisite for the later reporting, trend analysis and predictive capability described in Future Improvements.
61	
62	## Proposed Solution
63	
64	*How are we going to do it?*
65	
66	Rebuild the SLSA Surf Risk Rating experience natively within LIMSOC. LIMSOC provides the form and the workflow; the SLSA Surf Risk Rating API provides the score, rating and mitigation list. We are recreating the experience of a research-backed tool inside LIMSOC, not building the engine behind it. Access to the SLSA API and its request/response contract is a delivery dependency (see Assumptions and Configuration requirements).
67	
68	The first pass (v1) will:
69	
70	- Capture the inputs required by the SLSA SRR API, including locally observed environmental hazards.
71	- Prefill and augment those inputs with automated weather data from the Bureau of Meteorology (BOM) for the location nearest the unit.
72	- Submit the inputs to the SLSA API and return the score, rating and mitigation list it provides.
73	- Persist the completed assessment in LIMSOC and link it (many-to-one) to a patrol/unit.
74	- Make each assessment reviewable from patrol, field and dispatch views.
75	- Include the SRR in the patrol report and allow export of an individual SRR.
76	- Block the form when the SLSA API is not healthy (see Assumptions).
77	
78	Notifications, aggregation, map display and predictive modelling are deferred to later phases (see Future Improvements).
79	
80	## Assumptions
81	
82	*What must hold true for this feature to work as described. Several centre on the SLSA API, which is the scoring engine.*
83	
84	- **SLSA owns the engine; LIMSOC owns the form and the record.** LIMSOC does not build or hold the scoring logic. The form collects the inputs, passes them to the SLSA API, and the SLSA API returns the score, rating and mitigation list. LIMSOC then owns persistence of that result and the link to a patrol.
85	- **The SLSA API returns the score, rating and mitigation list.** The response contains all three, so LIMSOC does not need to derive any of them.
86	- **The SLSA API is performant and reliable.** This is assumed but not proven. SLSA has a history of APIs that are neither, so this assumption carries material risk and drives the fail-behaviour below.
87	- **A health-check endpoint is available on the SLSA API.** LIMSOC can query it to determine availability before allowing an assessment.
88	- **Fail behaviour: the form is blocked without a healthy SLSA response.** If the health check fails or the API does not return a healthy response, the assessment form is blocked and a clear unavailable state is shown. LIMSOC does not accept an assessment it cannot score, so no un-scored or locally-guessed assessments are recorded.
89	
90	## Functional Requirements
91	
92	*What the system does. Primary = first pass (v1). Secondary = phase 2. Tertiary = future.*
93	
94	### Primary (v1 - first pass)
95	
96	- Provide a capture form that collects the inputs required by the SLSA SRR API. Minimise friction: automate wherever possible, prefill from data already captured, and use engagement/gamification to encourage completion.
97	- Prefill and augment those inputs with BOM weather data for the location nearest the unit.
98	- Submit the collected inputs to the SLSA API and retrieve the score, rating and mitigation list it returns. LIMSOC does not compute the score.
99	- **Check SLSA API health before an assessment can be started, and block the form if a healthy response is not returned.** Do not allow an assessment to be completed without a live SLSA scoring response. Surface a clear unavailable state to the member.
100	- Give each assessment a geospatial position.
101	- Persist the completed assessment (inputs, and the returned score, rating and mitigants) in LIMSOC and link it (many-to-one) to a patrol/unit.
102	- Make each assessment reviewable from **patrol, field and dispatch** views.
103	- Present the mitigants returned by the SLSA API for the resulting rating, listed at the end of the assessment, presented like the Stinger Log.
104	- Include the SRR in the patrol report.
105	- Export an individual SRR.
106	- **Feature flag:** a general on/off flag for the feature (see Configuration).
107	- **Per-patrol-type enablement:** enable or disable the feature by patrol type (see Configuration).
108	- Where enabled and not yet completed, show the unit in an alert colour until an assessment has been logged for that unit for the patrol period.
109	
110	### Secondary (phase 2)
111	
112	- Augment observed data with additional internal LIMSOC data (for example Stinger Logs and similar), beyond BOM.

input.old_string:

LIMSOC does not accept an assessment it cannot score, so no un-scored or locally-guessed assessments are recorded.

1	# LIMSOC FEATURE BRIEF
2	
3	## Surf Risk Rating in LIMSOC
4	
5	| Field | Detail |
6	|---|---|
7	| **Brief number** | LIMSOC-BRIEF-LSV-2026-005 |
8	| **Version** | 2.0 (redraft) |
9	| **Author** | Flynn Young |
10	| **Revised by** | Nicholas Wood (State Lifesaving Communications Officer) |
11	| **Date** | 01/07/2026 |
12	
13	---
14	
15	## Sign off
16	
17	**Feature category: 3 - Moderate Business Impact.** 
18	
19	- 1 - Critical Operational Risk
20	- 2 - High Impact, Recoverable
21	- **3 - Moderate Business Impact** *(selected)*
22	- 4 - Low Operational Risk
23	- 5 - No Operational Dependency
24	
25	| Role | Name | Date |
26	|---|---|---|
27	| Feature owner | _____________________ | |
28	| Senior Manager - Capability | David Potter | |
29	| State Lifesaving Communications Officer | Nicholas Wood | |
30	
31	---
32	
33	## Overview
34	
35	*High-level statement outlining the feature and any relevant background information.*
36	
37	The Surf Risk Rating (SRR) is an established, research-backed SLSA assessment that members already use. Today it lives in the SLSA Operations App, and that solution no longer meets our operational needs. It is not native to LIMSOC, it is unreliable, and the result cannot flow into our operational workflows and data.
38	
39	SLSA has recently released an SRR API. This project uses that newly released API to build a native SRR experience within LIMSOC, giving members a cohesive experience and integrating the assessment into operational workflows.
40	
41	## Problem Statement
42	
43	*What problem are we solving?*
44	
45	Members currently complete the Surf Risk Rating in the SLSA Operations App, separate from LIMSOC. That leaves three problems:
46	
47	- **Not native to LIMSOC.** The assessment lives in a separate app, degrading the user experience and keeping it outside the workflows members already use.
48	- **The Operations App is unreliable.** Members cannot depend on the current tool being available or working when they need it.
49	- **Data is not tracable**: The data is not persisted in an accessible way. It is not retained against a patrol, and off-beach roles (field, dispatch, duty officers) cannot see whether an assessment was completed or what it found.
50	- **The score is not accessible to operational workflows.** The result cannot flow into LIMSOC operational workflows, reporting or data. 
51	
52	In short, we cannot capture the SRR natively, rely on it, or use the score in our operational workflows and data.
53	
54	## Impact
55	
56	*Impact of solving the problem, including the impact if left unaddressed.*
57	
58	- **Integrate risk assessment into operational workflows.** Bringing the SRR into LIMSOC lets the score plug into operational workflows. This makes the assessment easier for the member while better facilitating risk-management SOPs, so it has a direct impact on how we manage operational risk.
59	- **Drive adoption and integration.** A native, low-friction experience embedded in existing patrol workflows increases uptake of the SRR and makes it part of how patrols already work, rather than a separate step.
60	- **Give off-beach roles visibility.** Field, dispatch and duty roles gain sight of local risk and of whether an assessment has been completed for each unit. This is the primary situational-awareness win, and it lands with members who are not on the beach.
61	- **Make risk assessment traceable and documented.** The feature does not change how we operate, but it makes the assessment persistent, reviewable and auditable rather than transient. In practice it will also mean many more people use the SRR.
62	- **Build the data foundation.** A retained, structured record is the prerequisite for the later reporting, trend analysis and predictive capability described in Future Improvements.
63	
64	## Proposed Solution
65	
66	*How are we going to do it?*
67	
68	Build a native SRR experience in LIMSOC on top of the SLSA API. LIMSOC provides the form, the workflow and the record. The SLSA API provides the score, rating and mitigation list. Access to the SLSA API and its contract is a delivery dependency (see Assumptions and Configuration requirements).
69	
70	The first pass (v1) will:
71	
72	- Capture the inputs required by the SLSA SRR API, including locally observed environmental hazards.
73	- Prefill and augment those inputs with automated weather data from the Bureau of Meteorology (BOM) for the location nearest the user.
74	- Submit the inputs to the SLSA API and return the score, rating and mitigation list it provides.
75	- Persist the completed assessment in LIMSOC and link it (many-to-one) to a patrol/unit.
76	- Make each assessment reviewable from patrol, field and dispatch views.
77	- Include the SRR in the patrol report and allow export of an individual SRR.
78	- Block the form when the SLSA API is not healthy (see Assumptions).
79	
80	Notifications, aggregation, map display and predictive modelling are deferred to later phases (see Future Improvements).
81	
82	## Assumptions
83	
84	*What must hold true for this feature to work as described. Several centre on the SLSA API, which is the scoring engine.*
85	
86	- **SLSA owns the scoring engine, and LIMSOC owns the form and the record.** LIMSOC collects the inputs, sends them to the SLSA API, and the API returns the score, rating and mitigation list. LIMSOC owns persistence of that result and the link to a patrol.
87	- **The SLSA API returns the score, rating and mitigation list.**
88	- **The SLSA API is performant and reliable.** SLSA has a history of APIs that are neither, so this is assumed, not proven.
89	- **A health-check endpoint is available on the SLSA API.**
90	
91	## Functional Requirements
92	
93	*What the system does. Primary = first pass (v1). Secondary = phase 2. Tertiary = future.*
94	
95	### Primary (v1 - first pass)
96	
97	- Provide a capture form that collects the inputs required by the SLSA SRR API. Minimise friction: automate wherever possible, prefill from data already captured, and use engagement/gamification to encourage completion.
98	- Prefill and augment those inputs with BOM weather data for the location nearest the unit.
99	- Submit the collected inputs to the SLSA API and retrieve the score, rating and mitigation list it returns. LIMSOC does not compute the score.
100	- **Check SLSA API health before an assessment can be started, and block the form if a healthy response is not returned.** Do not allow an assessment to be completed without a live SLSA scoring response. Surface a clear unavailable state to the member.
101	- Give each assessment a geospatial position.
102	- Persist the completed assessment (inputs, and the returned score, rating and mitigants) in LIMSOC and link it (many-to-one) to a patrol/unit.
103	- Make each assessment reviewable from **patrol, field and dispatch** views.
104	- Present the mitigants returned by the SLSA API for the resulting rating, listed at the end of the assessment, presented like the Stinger Log.
105	- Include the SRR in the patrol report.
106	- Export an individual SRR.
107	- **Feature flag:** a general on/off flag for the feature (see Configuration).
108	- **Per-patrol-type enablement:** enable or disable the feature by patrol type (see Configuration).
109	- Where enabled and not yet completed, show the unit in an alert colour until an assessment has been logged for that unit for the patrol period.
110	
111	### Secondary (phase 2)
112	
113	- Augment observed data with additional internal LIMSOC data (for example Stinger Logs and similar), beyond BOM.
114	- Generate notifications when a score is elevated or falls outside defined parameters. *(Parameters and "abnormal" to be defined in the phase 2 brief.)*
115	- Average scores across zone, then region, then state. *(To be defined against a clear, useful metric and outcome before committing.)*
116	- Display scores on unit modals, maps and summaries.
117	- Report on historic data and trends.
118	
119	### Tertiary (future)
120	
121	- Use forecast data to extrapolate future scores in a predictive nature.
122	- Weight impact using current and previous population trends for a location. *(Requires a data source and an agreed methodology.)*

=== Primary requirements ===
- Provide a capture form that collects the inputs required by the SLSA SRR API. Minimise friction: automate wherever possible, prefill from data already captured, and use engagement/gamification to encourage completion.

- Export an individual SRR.

message.content: Rather than enabled or disabled, can it be updated to be required or optional. If required they MUST do it as part of the activity, if optional they cannot. The other things we need to cover in the first pass is if an SRR is complete while no activity is signed on. Once the SRR is completed, give them an option to link it to a signed on activity, if there is nothing signed on, prompt them to sign on. If they select do not link to an activity, this SRR should be logged against the unit they are signed in as (they can't access it without going through a unit.). So if an SRR is done as part of an activity, it should be linked to a UNIT and an ACTIVITY. (The unit will be implied by the activity). If is is not done sa part of an activity, it is just associated with the unit. The entry in the comm log should reflect this. When signing on an activity, there should be an option to link an existing SRR (i.e. they did the SRR before signing on). They should be able to choose from SRR completions for that unit, for that day, for the same activity. An SRR can only be linked to a max of one activity. Add a note that adding an SRR to multiple activities would be incorrect because participants is a factor in the rating and would be different between activities, other factors may also be different. Within the requirements, I think we may need to split it into categories 1. Completing and reviewing the form, everything in atrol view 2. Integrating it into workflows, 3. Notifications 4. Discoverability (Seeing it outside patrol view). A reqwuirement there is that there should be full assisted workflow (can be done over radio and completed from LSV Comms view). There then should be requirements around notifications. If a SRR is above a given score (threshold configurable), there should be a dangerous conditions incident opened. This should comply with our externally created incident workflow. The score for this should be configurable. (i.e. what score triggers an incident). If a dangerous conditions incident is already opened with the relevant unit attached to it, do not create another incident, just put a log note in that incident. Notifications for a dnagerous rating will be triggered off the incident and is out of scope for this feature.
