=== all FR-x.y.z cross-references that appear OUTSIDE their own definition line (i.e. in prose) ===
70:- **User satisfaction: a positive average experience score.** Measured from the experience score members give on completing an SRR (FR-1.1.23). Target to be set, for example an average of at least 4 out of 5.
275:- **Connection resilience.** The web form runs its logic client-side and remains usable through intermittent connectivity. A connection is required only at submit, to score via the SLSA API and to persist. Progress is not saved before submit (see FR-1.1.14 to FR-1.1.16).
279:- **Access control.** SRR visibility follows the view: patrol view is gated on the Surf Risk Rating (Online Modules) qualification (FR-1.1.18), while Field and Comms views are not (FR-1.4.7). Deletion is restricted to admin portal members (FR-1.2.19).
290:| 2. Build v1 | The Phase 1 requirements (FR-1.1.x, FR-1.2.x, FR-1.4.x): capture form, location select, BOM prefill, SLSA submit/retrieve, health-check and block, connection-resilient no-autosave form, persistence, unit/activity linking, required/optional sign-on gating, patrol-view module gate, review and menus, assisted Comms workflow, patrol report, export | TBC |

=== current 1.2 requirement lines ===
214:- **FR-1.2.1** Persist the completed assessment (inputs, and the returned score, rating and mitigants) in LIMSOC.
215:- **FR-1.2.2** Link an SRR completed as part of an activity to that activity and its unit. The unit is implied by the activity.
216:- **FR-1.2.3** Associate an SRR not completed as part of an activity with the unit only. Every SRR has at least a unit, because a member reaches the SRR through a unit.
217:- **FR-1.2.4** On completing an SRR with no activity signed on, offer to link it to a signed-on activity.
218:- **FR-1.2.5** If nothing is signed on when an SRR is completed, prompt the member to sign on.
219:- **FR-1.2.6** If the member declines to link, log the SRR against the unit they are signed in as.
220:- **FR-1.2.7** When signing on to an activity, offer to link an existing SRR completed before sign-on.
221:- **FR-1.2.8** Restrict that link choice to SRR completions for the same unit, the same day, and the same activity.
222:- **FR-1.2.9** Link an SRR to at most one activity. Participant numbers are an input to the rating and differ between activities, and other inputs may differ too, so one SRR cannot be valid for more than one activity.
223:- **FR-1.2.10** Reflect the linking in the comm log entry, showing whether the SRR is against a unit only, or against a unit and an activity.
224:- **FR-1.2.11** When a new full SRR is submitted for a unit (an updated score), add a log entry to the general log.
225:- **FR-1.2.12** Provide a general on/off feature flag that governs whether the feature is available.
226:- **FR-1.2.13** Allow each activity type (patrol type) to be configured as SRR-required or SRR-optional.
227:- **FR-1.2.14** Where SRR is required for an activity type, block sign-on to an activity of that type until a valid SRR is completed or an existing valid SRR is linked. Sign-on is a blocking step and cannot proceed without it.
228:- **FR-1.2.15** Where SRR is optional, present the SRR but do not block sign-on.
229:- **FR-1.2.16** Include the SRR in the patrol report.
230:- **FR-1.2.17** Allow export of an individual SRR.
231:- **FR-1.2.18** Retain every submitted SRR. There is no delete in the app UI.
232:- **FR-1.2.19** Allow only admin portal members to delete an SRR. To supersede a score, a member submits a new SRR, which makes the previous one redundant.

file.content:
## Personas and User Stories

*Personas are drafted from current understanding. Items marked "confirm" need your input.*

**Personas**

- **Patrol Member** - completes SRRs from patrol view, on a mobile device on the beach.
- **Duty Officer (Field view)** - oversees units in the field and needs visibility of current risk.
- **Comms Operator (Comms view)** - coordinates from the operations centre with statewide visibility, and can complete an SRR on a patrol's behalf.
- **Administrator (Reporting)** - uses the admin portal for reporting and data management, and is the only role that can delete an SRR.

**User stories**

Patrol Member

- As a patrol member, I want to complete an SRR quickly from my patrol view, so that I can record current risk without leaving my workflow.
- As a patrol member, I want the location and weather prefilled, so that I do the least possible manual entry.
- As a patrol member, I want to complete the SRR before or during sign-on and link it to my activity, so that the assessment is tied to the right activity.
- As a patrol member on a required activity type, I want to be told I must complete an SRR before I can sign on, so that the assessment is a clear prerequisite.

Duty Officer (Field view)

- As a duty officer, I want to see the latest SRR score and rating for each unit, so that I have situational awareness of local risk without being on the beach.
- As a duty officer, I want to see the day's trend for a unit, so that I can tell whether conditions are worsening.

Comms Operator (Comms view)

- As a comms operator, I want to complete an SRR on a patrol's behalf, so that a unit without LIMSOC access is still covered.
- As a comms operator, I want statewide visibility of SRR scores, so that I can monitor risk across the state.
- As a comms operator, I want to see the day's SRRs for a unit as documentation, so that I can review what was assessed.

Administrator (Reporting)

- As an administrator, I want to report on SRR completion and linkage, so that I can measure adoption against our targets.
- As an administrator, I want to delete an erroneous SRR from the admin portal, so that bad data can be removed, noting there is no delete in the app UI.
- As an administrator, I want historic SRR data retained, so that reporting and later analysis are possible.
- As an administrator, I want SRR data available in patrol and incident report exports
- As an administrator, I want to be able to export an SRR report for a given entry.

33	## Overview
34	
35	*High-level statement outlining the feature and any relevant background information.*
36	
37	The Surf Risk Rating (SRR) is an established, research-backed SLSA assessment that members already use. Today it lives in the SLSA Operations App, and that solution no longer meets our operational needs. It is not native to LIMSOC, it is unreliable, and the result cannot flow into our operational workflows and data.
38	
39	SLSA has recently released an SRR API. This project uses that newly released API to build a native SRR experience within LIMSOC, giving members a cohesive experience and integrating the assessment into operational workflows.
40	
41	## Problem Statement
42	
43	*What problem are we solving?*
44	
45	Members currently complete the Surf Risk Rating in the SLSA Operations App, separate from LIMSOC. That leaves four problems:
46	
47	- **Not native to LIMSOC.** The assessment lives in a separate app, degrading the user experience and keeping it outside the workflows members already use.
48	- **The Operations App is unreliable.** Members cannot depend on the current tool being available or working when they need it.
49	- **Data is not traceable.** The data is not persisted in an accessible way. It is not retained against a patrol, and off-beach roles (field, dispatch, duty officers) cannot see whether an assessment was completed or what it found.
50	- **The score is not accessible to operational workflows.** The result cannot flow into LIMSOC operational workflows, reporting or data.
51	
52	In short, we cannot capture the SRR natively, rely on it, or use the score in our operational workflows and data.
53	
54	## Impact
55	
56	*Impact of solving the problem, including the impact if left unaddressed.*
57	
58	- **Integrate risk assessment into operational workflows.** Bringing the SRR into LIMSOC lets the score plug into operational workflows. This makes the assessment easier for the member while better facilitating risk-management SOPs, so it has a direct impact on how we manage operational risk.
59	- **Drive adoption and integration.** A native, low-friction experience embedded in existing patrol workflows increases uptake of the SRR and makes it part of how patrols already work, rather than a separate step.
60	- **Give off-beach roles visibility.** Field and dispatch users gain sight of local risk and of whether an assessment has been completed for each unit. This is the primary situational-awareness win, and it lands with members who are not on the beach.
61	- **Make risk assessment traceable and consistent.** We should already be using the SRR, so this feature does not introduce a new obligation. It makes the assessment persistent, reviewable and auditable rather than transient, embeds it in our existing flows, and drives more consistent use across units.
62	- **Build the data foundation.** A retained, structured record is the prerequisite for the later reporting, trend analysis and predictive capability described in Future Improvements.
63	
64	## Success Metrics
65	
66	*How we will know the first pass has succeeded.*
67	
68	- **Coverage: 100% of required-type activities have a valid SRR.** Every activity of a required activity type has a valid SRR (completed through to submission) linked to it.
69	- **Linkage: 80% of SRRs are linked to an activity or an incident.** The remainder may legitimately be unit-only, completed outside an activity or incident.
70	- **User satisfaction: a positive average experience score.** Measured from the experience score members give on completing an SRR (FR-1.1.23). Target to be set, for example an average of at least 4 out of 5.
71	
72	## Proposed Solution
73	
74	*How are we going to do it?*
75	
76	Build a native SRR experience in LIMSOC on top of the SLSA API. LIMSOC provides the form, the workflow and the record. The SLSA API provides the score, rating and mitigation list. Access to the SLSA API and its contract is a delivery dependency (see Assumptions and Configuration requirements).
77	
78	The first pass (v1) will:
79	
80	- Capture the inputs required by the SLSA SRR API, including locally observed environmental hazards.
81	- Determine the location from the user's GPS (falling back to the unit location), and prefill and augment the inputs with automated weather data from the Bureau of Meteorology (BOM) for that location.
82	- Submit the inputs to the SLSA API and return the score, rating and mitigation list it provides.
83	- Persist the completed assessment in LIMSOC and link it (many-to-one) to a patrol/activity.
84	- Make each assessment reviewable from patrol, field and comms views.
85	- Include the SRR in the patrol report and allow export of an individual SRR.
86	- Block the form when the SLSA API is not healthy (see Assumptions).
87	
88	Aggregation, map display, the Dangerous Conditions Incident trigger and predictive modelling are deferred to later phases. Notifications are out of scope (see Functional Requirements).

92	*What must hold true for this feature to work as described. Several centre on the SLSA API, which is the scoring engine.*
93	
94	- **SLSA owns the scoring engine, and LIMSOC owns the form and the record.** LIMSOC collects the inputs, sends them to the SLSA API, and the API returns the score, rating and mitigation list. LIMSOC owns persistence of that result and the link to a patrol/activity.
95	- **The SLSA API returns the score, rating and mitigation list.**
96	- **The SLSA API is performant and reliable.** SLSA has a history of APIs that are neither, so this is assumed, not proven.
97	- **A health-check endpoint is available on the SLSA API.**
98	- **The location set used for incidents is available to reuse for SRR.**
